name: Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
headline: Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
description: Two lattice 5-polytopes refute Payne’s printed totally mixed face claims: a disconnected, nonshellable order complex with rational Betti numbers (2,22).
abstract: For two polytopes, retain the faces of their Minkowski sum whose two canonical summands have positive dimensions and whose dimension is the sum of those dimensions. This is the definition in Payne’s printed Oberwolfach question. Let D be the standard four-simplex and I = [0,1]. For the full-dimensional lattice polytopes D × I and (−D) × I in ℝ⁵, the qualifying-face order complex is a disjoint union of two connected pure graphs, each with 50 vertices and 60 edges. Its rational Betti numbers are (2,22,0,…). Thus both printed assertions, shellability and the homology of a wedge of three-spheres, fail. The shared interval factor deliberately produces a nongeneric example. The argument concerns the printed additive-dimension definition; it does not settle shellability for the different mixed faces used in stable tropical intersections.
